title: Subeg Singh Rejects Conversion and Mounts the Torture Wheel

blocks.text: Brought before the nawab and threatened with death, Subeg Singh refuses to convert and treats apostasy as worse than bodily destruction. His answer frames martyrdom as fidelity to dharam, not as a tragic accident, and it denies the court the moral satisfaction of thinking fear can purchase assent.

The authorities then bind him to the torture wheel, but even there he continues to invoke Akal and remember Guru Nanak rather than bargain for release. The page presents physical torment and spiritual steadiness side by side so that the violence of the regime only clarifies the firmness of the Sikh prisoner.

By the end of the scene, the nawab has failed to shake Subeg Singh through threat alone and begins looking for new methods of pressure. That shift prepares the next escalation, in which cruelty is redirected toward the martyr's family.
